verdict.rationale: Mastercard documents a quick-start guide where you create a Sandbox project, which grants the non-billable Test Drive plan covering all endpoints. Credentials (Partner ID, secret, appKey) are used to mint access tokens, and test FinBanks and personas let you link sandbox accounts via Connect. Client libraries are only generated from the OpenAPI spec in a GitHub repo, not shipped as official per-language SDKs, and self-serve key issuance and the speed of the flow are only implied. missing for 10: explicit self-serve instant key provisioning, a runnable end-to-end quickstart sample, official prebuilt per-language client libraries, independent hands-on corroboration of time-to-first-link.

support.subject: As a developer, I can go from signup to my first linked sandbox account fast — self-serve API keys, a runnable quickstart, and client libraries in my language

citations.quote: A Sandbox project gives you access to the Open Finance Test Drive plan. Test Drive is a non-billable, unlimited plan that provides access to all Open Finance API endpoints.
To create a token, you are required to provide the PartnerID along with the corresponding secret and appKey.
you will learn how to use our test banks (FinBanks) and test payroll provider (FinPayroll).
link them to at least one account via Connect
The test project generates an API client library from the API specification like you would do in a real application
